_note: An equity share whose sale is recorded on a recognised stock exchange is a security listed in a recognised stock exchange in India, short-term if held for not more than twelve months immediately preceding the date of its transfer (D-305). TY 2025-26: Income-tax Act, 1961 s.2(42A) first proviso, as amended w.e.f. 23-7-2024 by the Finance (No. 2) Act, 2024 s.3(b) ("(other than a unit)" omitted; the base period twenty-four months), thc copy p.49 and egazette 2024/256436 p.17. TY 2026-27: Income-tax Act, 2025 s.2(101)(b)(i), egazette 2025/265620 p.20. No later amendment (Finance Act, 2025; Taxation Laws (Amendment) Act, 2025; Finance Act, 2026 searched). Every TY 2025-26 transfer falls after 23-7-2024, so the amended text alone governs that year. Listing is read from the sale: a sale recorded on NSE or BSE (the recognised exchanges, D-297) shows the share traded there at transfer, which this row reads as listed — a reading (D-305 C1): SCRA also lets an exchange permit trading in a security not listed on it. A sale with no recorded exchange, or another string, matches no row and the bucket is refused. The months are calendar months — long-term only after the same date twelve months on — by the owner's ruling D-303. Period of holding: a demerged lot carries the demerged company's date as recorded (Explanation 1(i)(g); s.2(101)(c)(B)(III)); a bonus lot is dated at the corporate action's ex-date, not its allotment (Explanation 1(i)(f); s.2(101)(c)(C)(IV)) until W-088k4. Sources: docs/taxplanning-build/sources/2026-10-21-holding-period.md rows 1–3, 4, 6–8, 10.
